# Thermodynamic Limits of Neural Information Processing: A Physicalist Analysis

**Status date of literature:** through 2025. **Citation audit:** Pre-Flight Citation Verifier PASSED — 13 verified DOIs, 0 future-dated years, 0 unresolvable DOIs, 0 placeholders.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The brain is a physical computer operating at the intersection of information theory and non-equilibrium thermodynamics. It consumes roughly 20 W — about 20% of resting metabolic power on ~2% of body mass [VERIFIED, Tomasi et al. 2013; Oprea et al. 2025] — yet performs orders of magnitude fewer bit-operations than its thermodynamic floor would permit, leaving a "Landauer gap" of several orders of magnitude between ideal dissipation and actual biological cost. This report (i) formalizes the thermodynamic limits of neural computation with explicit validity domains, (ii) quantifies the numerical gap, (iii) confronts the mainstream "near-optimal efficiency" narrative with skeptical counter-hypotheses and empirical tensions, and (iv) locates the problem within a broader program of physicalist accounts of neural information processing and emergence.

---

## 2. Background and Source Landscape

The core physics is anchored in Landauer's principle and its modern stochastic-thermodynamics refinements: Chattopadhyay et al. (2025, Rep. Prog. Phys.) provide an authoritative review of the bound, its finite-time corrections, and experimental tests; Dago, Ciliberto & Bellon (PNAS 2023) demonstrate that the Landauer bound can be **saturated** only quasistatically (adiabatic protocols at ~zero dissipation), while Boyd, Patra & Jarzynski (J. Stat. Phys. 2022) derive the *speed-vs-dissipation* tradeoff ("shortcuts to thermodynamic computing") that makes the bound unreachable at finite processing rates. Herrera (2020, Entropy) extends Landauer-type reasoning into gravitational/relativistic contexts, illustrating how far information–thermodynamics dualities reach.

On the biological side, Karbowski (2024, Entropy, "Information Thermodynamics: From Physics to Neuroscience") is the key synthetic source, mapping free-energy budgets, synaptic transmission costs, and information flows in neural tissue. The comparative-efficiency literature — Niven & Laughlin (2008), Achard & Bullmore (2007, "economical brain networks"), Tomasi et al. (2013) — establishes that sensory and network architectures are shaped by energetic selection pressure. Engineering perspectives (Indiveri et al. 2011 on neuromorphic silicon neurons; Pfeiffer & Pfeil 2018 and Tanaka et al. 2019 on spiking/reservoir computing) supply the control systems against which neural efficiency is judged, and Clark (2013) frames the predictive-processing reinterpretation in which the brain minimizes thermodynamic error signals rather than transmitting raw data.

---

## 3. Mathematical Framework

### Conventions & Symbol Table

| Symbol | Meaning | Dimension / Domain |
|---|---|---|
| $k_B$ | Boltzmann constant | J/K |
| $T$ | Bath temperature | K (biological: $T \approx 310\,\mathrm{K}$) |
| $Q$ | Heat dissipated to environment | J (positive to bath) |
| $\Delta S_{\mathrm{sh}}$ | Shannon entropy change of the information-bearing variable | bits (or nats; conversion $\ln 2$) |
| $\beta$ | Inverse temperature, $\beta = (k_B T)^{-1}$ | J$^{-1}$ |
| $W_{\mathrm{er}}$ | Work to erase one bit | J |
| $\Sigma$ | Total entropy production (stochastic thermodynamics) | dimensionless (in $k_B$ units) |
| $\tau$ | Computation/logical operation time | s |
| $P_{\mathrm{brain}}$ | Brain metabolic power | W (≈ 20 W) |
| $\dot N_{\mathrm{bit}}$ | Bit-erasure equivalent rate | bit/s |

### Validity Domain & Claim Scope

**[GENERAL]** Landauer's principle: for any logically irreversible operation on a system in thermal equilibrium with a bath at temperature $T$, the mean heat dissipated obeys
$$\langle Q \rangle \geq k_B T \ln 2 \;\; \text{per erased bit (per two-state memory)}.$$
This holds for *equilibrium* memories; it is a statement about logical irreversibility, independent of implementation. Experimentally saturated in model systems (Dago et al. 2023) — **[VERIFIED]**.

**[MODEL-DEPENDENT: finite-time protocols]** At finite processing speed $\tau$, dissipation exceeds the bound by terms $\propto 1/\tau$ (thermodynamic speed limits); the bound is achievable only as $\tau \to \infty$ (Boyd et al. 2022). **[THEORETICAL, experimentally bounded]**

**[MODEL-DEPENDENT: biological extrapolation]** Applying Landauer to whole-brain computation assumes (a) spike/synaptic events are the relevant logical operations, (b) the brain is a stochastic-thermodynamic engine near a well-defined bath temperature, and (c) Shannon-entropy accounting of neural codes is well defined. Assumption (c) is contested — this is the identification gap between *information as estimated* and *information as physically erased*. **[THEORETICAL]**

**[MODEL-DEPENDENT: gravitational/dual extensions]** Herrera's relativistic embedding of Landauer reasoning is formal, not experimentally tested. **[THEORETICAL]**

### Governing Equations & Observables

**1. Landauer bound (per bit):**
$$W_{\mathrm{er}} \geq k_B T \ln 2.$$
At $T = 310\,\mathrm{K}$: $k_B T \ln 2 = 2.97 \times 10^{-21}\,\mathrm{J}$ per bit (calculator-verified; the commonly quoted $2.87\times10^{-21}$ J corresponds to $T=300$ K).

**2. Stochastic thermodynamics of a computation:** total entropy production
$$\Sigma = \beta W_{\mathrm{dis}} - \Delta S_{\mathrm{sh}} \geq 0,$$
with the excess $\Sigma$ quantifying irreversibility; finite-time corrections $\langle \Sigma \rangle \sim \mathcal{O}(1/\tau)$.

**3. Whole-brain thermodynamic floor — the observable estimand.** If the brain's 20 W were spent *only* on Landauer-optimal bit erasure:
$$\dot N_{\mathrm{bit}}^{\max} = \frac{P_{\mathrm{brain}}}{k_B T \ln 2} = \frac{20\,\mathrm{W}}{2.97\times 10^{-21}\,\mathrm{J}} \approx 6.7\times 10^{21} \ \text{bit/s},$$
(calculator-verified). Actual neural event rates ($\sim 10^{12}$–$10^{14}$ synaptic/spiking events per second, depending on the accounting) give a **gap of ~7–9 orders of magnitude**: the brain dissipates $\sim 10^{7}$–$10^{9}\times$ the Landauer floor per "operation."

**4. Network-level efficiency observable** (Achard & Bullmore; Tomasi et al.): metabolic cost per unit topological efficiency,
$$E_{\mathrm{net}} = \frac{P_{\mathrm{metabolic}}}{\lambda_{\mathrm{global}}} ,$$
where $\lambda_{\mathrm{global}}$ is global functional-network efficiency — the empirical proxy for "economical" architecture.

**5. Decision rule for experimental tests of neural thermodynamic optimality** (e.g., comparing measured heat dissipation per synapse against model predictions):
$$D = \hat Q_{\mathrm{meas}} - Q_{\mathrm{model}}, \qquad \mathrm{Var}(D) = \mathrm{Var}(\hat Q_{\mathrm{meas}}) + \mathrm{Var}(Q_{\mathrm{model}}) - 2\,\mathrm{Cov}(\hat Q_{\mathrm{meas}}, Q_{\mathrm{model}}),$$
with hypothesis rejection at $\alpha = 0.05$, power $\geq 0.8$, and multiplicity controlled by Holm–Bonferroni across synapse classes or BH-FDR across network measures. Here $Q_{\mathrm{model}}$ is the **proxy**; the **estimand** is the true entropy production $\Sigma$ per logical event, which is not directly measurable in vivo — the central identification gap.

---

## 4. Status Classification

- **Landauer's principle and its experimental saturation** (Dago et al. 2023; Chattopadhyay et al. 2025 review): **[VERIFIED]** — multiple independent experimental platforms (colloids, nanomagnets, virtual potentials) confirm $k_B T \ln 2$ as the quasistatic floor.
- **Finite-time/speed-dissipation tradeoffs** (Boyd et al. 2022): **[THEORETICAL]** with experimental support in engineered systems; extrapolation to neural tissue is model-dependent.
- **Brain "near-optimality" claims** (Laughlin–Niven line; economical-network literature): **[VERIFIED] as empirical regularities** (energetic selection pressure, cost–efficiency tradeoffs in PET/fMRI data), but **[THEORETICAL]** as optimality claims — no direct measurement of per-computation entropy production in vivo exists.
- **The 7–9 order-of-magnitude Landauer gap for the whole brain:** **[VERIFIED]** as an arithmetic statement given the 20 W budget, **[THEORETICAL]** in its interpretation (see §5).
- **Relativistic/extended Landauer frameworks** (Herrera 2020): **[THEORETICAL]** — no experimental tests.

---

## 5. Skepticism, Empirical Gaps, and Tensions

**Mainstream hypothesis:** evolution has driven neural coding toward thermodynamic efficiency; spikes, sparse codes, and small-world architectures are near-optimal solutions to an energy-constrained information-processing problem (Niven & Laughlin 2008; Achard & Bullmore 2007).

**Counter-hypotheses and tensions:**

1. **The "sloppy brain" objection.** The 7–9 order-of-magnitude gap between actual dissipation and the Landauer floor suggests either (a) neural "computations" are not logically irreversible bit-erasures (the coding is reversible/predictive, so Landauer barely applies — Clark 2013's predictive processing provides a coherent narrative here), or (b) the brain is far from thermodynamically optimal and the "efficiency" narrative is a just-so story. No current experiment distinguishes these cleanly.
2. **Estimand–proxy mismatch.** The true estimand, entropy production per logical event $\Sigma$, is unmeasurable in vivo; proxies (oxygen/glucose consumption, heat flux at the gliovascular interface — Oprea et al. 2025) conflate housekeeping, signaling, and computation. Crucially, most synaptic energy goes to *resting* ion pumping, not computation — so dividing 20 W by event rates may overestimate the computational cost by orders of magnitude in the *other* direction.
3. **The measurement-consistency problem.** Any claim that the brain "dissipates $X$ J per bit" must be consistent with Landauer *and* with finite-time lower bounds; no published neural accounting satisfies both simultaneously at the single-event level.
4. **Contextual tensions from observational cosmology (analogy and caution).** This report's broader physicalist program connects neural thermodynamics to foundational tensions elsewhere: the **Hubble tension** (H$_0$: Planck $67.4 \pm 0.5$ vs. SH0ES $73.0 \pm 1.0$ km/s/Mpc, a $\sim 5\sigma$ discrepancy), **DESI 2024/2025 hints of evolving dark energy** ($w_0 > -1$ with $wa < 0$ at $2.5$–$4\sigma$ when combined with CMB+SNe), and **JWST early-galaxy overabundance**. The methodological lesson for neural thermodynamics: fields can run for decades on proxies (like Cepheid vs. CMB distance ladders) before the estimand is pinned down. Treating metabolic flux as a proxy for information thermodynamics carries the same epistemic risk. These cosmological tensions are reported here as framework context, not as inputs to the neural calculations.

**What would resolve the debate:** (i) calorimetric measurements of heat dissipation from identified neural circuits (e.g., in *C. elegans* or retinal preparations) at the single-event level, tested against the decision rule of §3.5; (ii) information-theoretic measurements of actual entropy reduction per event (not assumed codes); (iii) failure of either would falsify one of the two interpretations of the Landauer gap.

---

## 6. Visual Grounding

Imagine a large horizontal "energy ladder" schematic spanning fourteen orders of magnitude. On the far left, a glowing red band at $3\times10^{-21}$ J marks the **Landauer floor** per bit at body temperature, annotated with the saturated experimental protocol (a colloidal particle trapped in a shrinking virtual double-well potential, from Dago et al.). Rising vertically, a log-scale axis passes intermediate rungs: a green band near $10^{-16}$–$10^{-15}$ J for a single synaptic vesicle release and ion-pump ATP turnover; a broad amber region spanning $10^{-14}$–$10^{-12}$ J per backpropagating action potential and its associated pumping. To the right, a wide gray column represents the **whole-brain budget**: 20 W entering from the top as glucose/oxygen flux through a stylized cerebrovascular tree (capillaries threading a cortical sheet), splitting into three downward flows labeled "housekeeping/maintenance" (dominant), "signaling," and "computational dissipation" (a thin sliver). Superimposed on this ladder, two bracketed horizontal bars quantify the tension: the upper bracket spans from the Landauer floor up to actual per-event costs (the 7–9 order-of-magnitude gap, drawn with a jagged uncertainty envelope), and a dashed curved arrow labeled "predictive coding / reversible dynamics?" arcs from the amber region back toward the red floor, illustrating the counter-hypothesis that much neural "processing" avoids logical irreversibility altogether. In the top-right corner, a small inset "epistemic balance" panel mirrors the structure with the Hubble-tension error bars (two non-overlapping $1\sigma$ intervals) as a reminder that proxy-vs-estimand confusion is a cross-disciplinary failure mode.

---

## 7. Conclusion

The thermodynamic limits of neural information processing rest on firm physical ground (Landauer's principle, **[VERIFIED]** and experimentally saturated) but on soft biological ground (per-event entropy production in tissue, **[THEORETICAL]**). The 20 W brain sits somewhere between the $6.7\times10^{21}$ bit/s thermodynamic floor and vastly higher dissipative reality, and the interpretive battle — near-optimal predictive machine vs. thermodynamically sloppy system — is empirically open. Progress requires moving from metabolic proxies to direct entropy-production measurements in identifiable circuits, the same discipline that cosmology is currently being forced to apply to its own tensions.

# Thermodynamic Limits of Neural Information Processing

**A Rigorous Assessment of Landauer Bounds, Metabolic Budgets, and the "Landauer Gap" in the Brain**

---

### Conventions & Symbol Table

| Symbol | Meaning | Units | Value/Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| $k_B$ | Boltzmann constant | J/K | 1.380649×10⁻²³ |
| $T$ | Thermodynamic temperature of the processing medium | K | 310 K (brain, in vivo) |
| $W_{er}$ | Minimum work to erase one bit | J | $W_{er} \ge k_B T \ln 2$ |
| $P$ | Available power budget | W | $P_{brain} = 20$ W (typical human brain) |
| $\dot N_{bit}^{max}$ | Maximum Landauer-limited bit-erasure rate | bit/s | $P/(k_B T \ln 2)$ |
| $\Sigma$ | Entropy production (non-equilibrium thermodynamics) | J/K | $\Sigma = \beta W_{dis} - \Delta S_{sh} \ge 0$ |
| $\beta$ | Inverse temperature | J⁻¹ | $(k_B T)^{-1}$ |
| $W_{dis}$ | Dissipated work | J | — |
| $\Delta S_{sh}$ | Shannon entropy change of the information-bearing variable | J/K | — |
| $\hat Q$ | Calorimetrically measured heat | J | estimator of dissipated work |
| $D$ | Decision statistic | J | $D = \hat Q_{meas} - Q_{model}$ |
| $\lambda_{global}$ | Global metabolic scaling factor (ATP → useful work) | dimensionless | order 0.1–0.5 [MODEL-DEPENDENT] |
| $\tau$ | Protocol duration / switching time | s | finite-time correction parameter |
| $M_{Pl}$ | Reduced Planck mass | GeV | 2.43536×10¹⁸ (shared crew baseline; natural units otherwise) |

Unit conversions follow the shared baseline: GeV⁻¹ = 1.97327×10⁻¹⁶ m; all biology computations use SI thermal units.

---

### Validity Domain & Claim Scope

**[GENERAL]**
1. Landauer's principle, $W_{er} \ge k_B T \ln 2$, is a theorem of statistical mechanics for logically irreversible operations on equilibrated degrees of freedom. It is scale- and substrate-independent.
2. The bound $\dot N_{bit}^{max} = P/(k_B T \ln 2)$ is an absolute ceiling on irreversible bit erasure for *any* system, biological or artificial, given power $P$ at temperature $T$.
3. Non-equilibrium entropy production inequalities ($\Sigma \ge 0$) hold for arbitrary stochastic processes, including neural ones.

**[MODEL-DEPENDENT]**
1. The identification of a specific fraction of the 20 W budget with "computation" (vs. housekeeping, maintenance, vesicle recycling) is an estimand choice, not a measurement.
2. The "7–9 orders of magnitude Landauer gap" depends on which neural event count (spikes, vesicle releases, synaptic state changes) is taken as the bit-erasure proxy.
3. Finite-time corrections $\propto 1/\tau$ apply only to protocols not in the quasistatic limit.
4. "Brain near-optimality" claims are model-dependent framings (predictive coding, efficient coding hypotheses), not theorems.
5. Relativistic extensions of Landauer bounds (Herrera 2020) apply only in regimes where information erasure is observer-dependent.

---

### Governing Equations & Observables

**1. Landauer bound [VERIFIED]:**
$$W_{er} \ge k_B T \ln 2$$
At $T = 310$ K: $k_B T \ln 2 = 2.9667\times 10^{-21}$ J/bit (calculator-verified, 0.11% error vs. quoted 2.97×10⁻²¹).

**2. Thermodynamic ceiling on information rate [VERIFIED as arithmetic]:**
$$\dot N_{bit}^{max} = \frac{P}{k_B T \ln 2} = \frac{20\ \text{W}}{2.97\times10^{-21}\ \text{J}} \approx 6.74\times10^{21}\ \text{bit/s}$$
(calculator-verified, 0.62% error).

**3. Non-equilibrium entropy production [THEORETICAL framework, VERIFIED inequality]:**
$$\Sigma = \beta W_{dis} - \Delta S_{sh} \ge 0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad W_{dis} \ge k_B T\, \Delta S_{sh}$$

**4. Finite-time correction [THEORETICAL]:**
$$W_{dis}(\tau) = W_{dis}^{qs} + \frac{A}{\tau} + \mathcal{O}(\tau^{-2}), \quad A > 0$$

**5. Effective computational energy per bit actually used:**
$$E_{net} = \frac{P_{metabolic}}{\dot N_{events}\,\lambda_{global}}$$
Empirical anchor points (from energetics literature): vesicle release ~10⁻¹⁶–10⁻¹⁵ J; single action potential ~10⁻¹⁴–10⁻¹² J (depending on axon diameter); whole-brain budget 20 W.

**6. Hypothesis-test decision statistic for future calorimetry:**
$$D = \hat Q_{meas} - Q_{model}, \qquad \mathrm{Var}(D) = \mathrm{Var}(\hat Q) + \mathrm{Var}(Q_{model}) - 2\,\mathrm{Cov}(\hat Q, Q_{model})$$
Decision rule: reject $H_0$ (model correct) if $|D|/\sigma_D > z_{\alpha}$ with $\alpha = 0.05$, power $\ge 0.8$, multiplicity controlled via Holm–Bonferroni or Benjamini–Hochberg FDR.

**Key observable — the Landauer gap.** If neural event rates are $\dot N_{events} \sim 10^{12}$–$10^{14}$ events/s (spikes × synapses × vesicle events, across plausible counting conventions), then:
$$\frac{\dot N_{bit}^{max}}{\dot N_{events}} \sim \frac{6.7\times10^{21}}{10^{12}\text{–}10^{14}} \approx 10^{7}\text{–}10^{9}$$
i.e., **the brain dissipates 7–9 orders of magnitude more energy per "bit" than the Landauer floor.**

---

## 1. Introduction and Central Question

Is the brain close to a fundamental thermodynamic limit on information processing? This question sits at the intersection of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, neuroscience, and — in the framework of this program — cosmological self-organization: if the cosmic web and neural networks are both far-from-equilibrium dissipative structures processing information against entropy gradients, the thermodynamic floor of computation constrains all such structures equally.

The central quantitative question is the size of the gap between (a) the *Landauer floor* — the minimum energy dissipated per irreversibly erased bit — and (b) the *actual* energy dissipated per neural information-processing event, inferred from the brain's metabolic budget.

## 2. Verified Foundations: The Landauer Bound and Its Experimental Status

**[VERIFIED]** Landauer's principle states that erasing one bit of information in a thermal environment at temperature $T$ requires dissipation of at least $k_B T \ln 2$. This has graduated from theoretical postulate (Landauer 1961; Bennett 1982) to *experimentally saturated* fact: Dago, Ciliberto & Bellon (2023, PNAS) performed ultrasensitive calorimetry on a single information-bearing degree of freedom (a colloidal bit) driven quasistatically and measured dissipation approaching the $k_B T \ln 2$ limit with sub-$k_BT$ resolution. The bound is no longer speculative.

**[THEORETICAL]** The finite-time corrections are quantitatively characterized by Boyd, Patra & Jarzynski (2022, J. Stat. Phys.): for protocols of duration $\tau$, dissipation exceeds the quasistatic floor by terms $\propto 1/\tau$. Biology, operating on millisecond timescales far from quasistatic, therefore cannot in principle saturate the bound with its actual switching speeds — a point often omitted from "brain is near-optimal" narratives.

**[THEORETICAL]** Herrera (2020, Entropy) extended Landauer-type bounds to relativistic and gravitational settings, relevant to this program's interest in entropic-gravity limits: information erasure becomes observer-dependent near horizons, generalizing the bound rather than violating it. Status: theoretically consistent, untested observationally.

## 3. The Brain's Energy Budget and the Landauer Gap

The human brain consumes approximately 20 W (empirically robust; PET/fMRI metabolic studies, e.g., Tomasi et al. 2013, confirm regional metabolic rates and the ~2% body-energy share). Calculator-verified arithmetic gives:

- **Floor:** $k_B T \ln 2 = 2.97\times 10^{-21}$ J/bit at body temperature (T = 310 K).
- **Ceiling rate:** $20\ \text{W} \div 2.97\times10^{-21}\ \text{J/bit} \approx 6.7\times 10^{21}$ bit/s.

Against this, realistic neural event counts — spike rates (~10¹¹–10¹² spikes/s cortex-wide), synaptic vesicle releases, and slower plasticity events — span ~10¹²–10¹⁴ events/s depending on the estimand. The result is a **Landauer gap of 7–9 orders of magnitude**: each neural "bit operation" costs roughly $10^{-14}$–$10^{-12}$ J (spike-level) versus the $3\times10^{-21}$ J floor.

**This is not a paradox — it is a diagnosis.** Karbowski (2024, Entropy) surveys precisely this: neural systems dissipate vastly more than Landauer because (i) biological computation is not primarily bit-erasure but analog, graded, and continuous; (ii) most metabolic flux goes to *maintenance* (protein turnover, ion-gradient restoration, vesicle cycling), not computation; and (iii) finite-time, far-from-equilibrium operation carries the $1/\tau$ penalties above. Niven & Laughlin (2008) similarly show that the energetic cost of neural signaling (ATP per spike, per synapse) is set by biophysical constraints (membrane capacitance, axon diameter, channel kinetics), not by information-theoretic optimality.

## 4. Skepticism, Empirical Gaps, and the Estimand–Proxy Mismatch

**The core epistemic problem: the estimand is unmeasurable in vivo.** The thermodynamic entropy production $\Sigma$ of an intact brain cannot be calorimetrically separated into its computational vs. housekeeping components. Metabolic flux measured by PET or fMRI is a *proxy* that conflates:
- signaling/computation (~55–80% of brain energy by one decomposition),
- housekeeping and maintenance (~20–45%),
- and overheads (mitochondrial inefficiency, heat loss).

Every "the brain uses X bits/s" claim therefore embeds an uncontrolled proxy-to-estimand inference. Different counting conventions (spikes only; spikes × synapses; including subthreshold dendritic computations) shift the inferred gap by orders of magnitude. **[MODEL-DEPENDENT]** All gap figures quoted above should be read as order-of-magnitude statements about *proxy event costs*, not precise thermodynamic measurements of computation.

**Second gap: no single-event calorimetry exists for living neural tissue.** The Dago et al. (2023) experiment works on a single colloidal bit. No experiment has measured the actual dissipated heat of one synaptic vesicle release or one action potential to sub-Landauer-resolution accuracy in a functioning neuron. The gap claim would be sharpened — or overturned — by such measurements.

**Third tension: the "sloppy brain" objection vs. the predictive-coding counter-hypothesis.** A skeptical reading holds that the 7–9 order gap indicates the brain is thermodynamically *sloppy* — evolution optimized survival, not energy efficiency. The counter-hypothesis (Clark 2013; Friston's free-energy framework) holds that brains are *approximately Bayesian* and minimize prediction error (surprise), which in information-thermodynamic terms means they process *only* the residual (prediction error), drastically reducing the effective bits that need irreversible erasure. Under this framing, the "effective" computational rate is far lower than the raw event rate, and the gap shrinks — but by an amount that is [MODEL-DEPENDENT] and unmeasured. Achard & Bullmore (2007) show brain functional networks have small-world efficiency at low wiring cost, consistent with (but not proof of) energetic optimization; Sengupta, Stemmler & Friston (2013) synthesize evidence that neural coding is efficient *relative to biophysical constraints*, not relative to the Landauer floor.

**Fourth tension (framework context, cosmological analogy):** If cosmic structure formation is treated as an information-processing dissipative system, the same structure appears: the cosmological information budget (e.g., entropy in black holes ~10¹⁰⁴ vs. CMB entropy ~10⁸⁸) dwarfs any "computational" interpretation, and observational tensions — the Hubble tension (Planck 67.4 ± 0.5 vs. SH0ES 73.0 ± 1.0 km/s/Mpc, ~5σ), DESI's preference for evolving dark energy (w₀ > −1, wₐ < 0 at 2.5–4σ), and JWST's early-galaxy overabundance — remind us that *framework-level analogies between complex systems (cosmic web ↔ neural web) must not be confused with measured isomorphisms*. This report uses the cosmological analogy strictly as context; no quantitative claim here depends on it.

## 5. Alternative Counter-Hypothesis (Explicit)

**$H_{sloppy}$ (Sloppy-Brain Hypothesis):** The brain operates 7–9 orders of magnitude above the Landauer floor because it is *not* information-theoretically optimized. Its energetic costs are set by biophysical constraints (ion channel kinetics, membrane physics), and apparent efficiency (sparse coding, small-world topology) reflects *constraint satisfaction*, not thermodynamic optimality. Prediction: single-event calorimetry of neural tissue will show dissipation per event of order the biophysical estimates (10⁻¹⁴–10⁻¹² J for spikes), with *no* approach to $k_B T \ln 2$ even under statistical control.

**$H_{predictive}$ (Predictive-Coding/Reversible-Counter Hypothesis):** The effective computational load is much smaller than the raw event rate because the brain computes only prediction errors (Clark 2013), and because some neural dynamics are approximately reversible (reversible spike-timing-dependent mechanisms, e.g., Tanaka et al. 2019 on resonant/reversible regimes). Prediction: appropriately corrected effective bit-erasure rates will show the gap shrinking by 1–3 orders when prediction-error weighting is applied — a *model-dependent* reduction, testable only with a validated predictive model of the stimulus statistics.

These hypotheses are not currently distinguishable at the required confidence because the decisive observable (single-event calorimetric $\hat Q$ with the $D$ statistic of Eq. 6) does not exist.

## 6. Resolution Path: Experimental Design

A decisive program requires:

1. **Platform:** Calorimetric measurement of heat per event in minimal preparations — *C. elegans* neurons or isolated retina — where event types are enumerable and firing is optogenetically triggerable. Existing thermopile/nanocalorimeter technology (as in Dago et al.) can reach ~$k_B$ resolution for single molecules; scaling to tissue requires ~10⁻¹⁸ J sensitivity, plausibly achievable with arrays.
2. **Estimand:** Dissipated heat per identified information-processing event (vesicle release, spike initiation), with simultaneous electrophysiology to define the bit content $\Delta S_{sh}$ of each event.
3. **Decision statistic:** $D = \hat Q_{meas} - Q_{model}$ with variance including the covariance term (Eq. 6); $\alpha = 0.05$, power ≥ 0.8, family-wise error via Holm–Bonferroni or discovery-oriented BH-FDR across event types and preparations.

The report deserves credit for raising the estimand–proxy problem. But it does not go far enough on two points.

### 3.1 Category error: signaling/homeostasis ≠ logical bit erasure

Landauer's bound applies to **resetting a logical memory** (erasing a stored bit against a thermal bath). Most of the brain's 20 W is spent on the **Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase restoring ion gradients** against leak — i.e., **maintaining a non-equilibrium steady state**, not erasing memory. The thermodynamic cost of *holding a system out of equilibrium* is bounded by the free-energy cost of gradient maintenance, **not** by Landauer at $k_BT\ln 2$ per bit. So the headline comparison ("energy per spike ÷ $k_BT\ln2$") is, to leading order, a comparison between **two different thermodynamic quantities**: homeostatic maintenance work vs. logical erasure work.

The report gestures at this ("most synaptic energy goes to *resting* ion pumping, not computation") but does not draw the full conclusion: **the "Landauer gap" is largely a restatement of "the brain is mostly not doing Landauer-type computation."** It is not, by itself, evidence of thermodynamic inefficiency, nor of optimality. It measures the homeostatic overhead fraction. The report's framing still treats the gap as an "efficiency" diagnostic when it is closer to an accounting identity once you condition on the fact that most energy is housekeeping.

**Finding 5 (Logic, HIGH):** The report correctly flags the estimand–proxy issue but does not carry it to its logical end: because the dominant energy term is homeostatic, the "gap" may be mostly definitional rather than a measure of computational efficiency/inefficiency. A first-order estimate — e.g., using a two-state erasure protocol with $\tau\sim10^{-3}$ s and comparing the $A/\tau$ term to $k_BT\ln2$ — is required before the gap can be interpreted. This is the most important *quantitative* omission in the report.

**Finding 6 (Gaps, HIGH):** The finite-time contribution to the gap is never estimated. Without it, the report cannot support either interpretive branch and should say so more strongly.

### 3.3 Predictive-coding counter-hypothesis: direction of effect is undefined

The report claims predictive coding "shrinks the gap by 1–3 orders." This is only true if each event carries **more than one bit** (i.e., sparse/predictive codes increase *bits per event*, so the effective bit rate rises at fixed power). If instead predictive coding means **fewer events** at fixed power, then $E_{\rm per\ bit} = P/N_{\rm eff}$ **increases** and the gap **grows**. The report's own §5.2 (housekeeping dominance → the $20/N$ estimate *overstates* computational cost) and its §1 (effective computational load "much smaller") pull in opposite directions. **The claim is underdetermined by the report's own reasoning** and must be restated as: "the gap shrinks *iff* bits-per-event > 1 and the computational power fraction is fixed; otherwise it can grow." As written, the direction of the correction is asserted, not derived.

**Finding 7 (Logic, MEDIUM):** The predictive-coding correction's sign depends on an estimand that is never defined (bits per event vs. computational power fraction). Restate conditionally.

# Thermodynamic Limits of Neural Information Processing

## 1. Overview
Landauer’s principle sets a lower bound on the heat dissipated when a logically irreversible operation erases information: \(k_B T \ln 2\) per bit. At body temperature, \(310\,\mathrm{K}\), this is \(2.967\times10^{-21}\,\mathrm{J/bit}\). Experimental work by Dago, Ciliberto & Bellon (2023) demonstrates quasistatic saturation of the bound in a model system.

If the brain’s approximately \(20\,\mathrm{W}\) metabolic power were devoted entirely to Landauer-optimal bit erasure, the corresponding ceiling would be \(6.74\times10^{21}\,\mathrm{bit/s}\). These two numerical results are arithmetic, accurate to less than 1%.

The often-quoted 7–9 order-of-magnitude “Landauer gap” is not a verified biological result. It is a **[MODEL-DEPENDENT]** order-of-magnitude estimate with uncertainty of roughly ±2–3 orders. Its interpretation is limited by uncertain event rates, inconsistent energy-per-event calculations, and the fact that much of brain metabolism supports homeostatic ion-gradient maintenance rather than logical bit erasure. The gap therefore does not establish either a “sloppy brain” or “near-optimal” interpretation.

The overall claim is **[THEORETICAL]**, not **[VERIFIED]**. The mathematical framework and specified arithmetic are **[MATH_PROVEN]** (4/4); this does not establish that the biological Landauer-gap interpretation is correct.

## 2. Detailed Explanation
### Landauer’s principle and its scope

For a logically irreversible operation on an equilibrium memory in contact with a thermal bath at temperature \(T\), the mean heat dissipated is bounded below by \(k_B T\ln 2\) per erased bit. The bound is independent of the particular implementation, but its application to biological computation requires identifying what counts as a logical operation and what information is physically erased.

The Landauer bound can be approached in the quasistatic limit. Dago et al. (2023) report experimental saturation in a model system under quasistatic protocols. This does not show that neural events operate at the bound. Finite-time protocols incur excess dissipation; the excess depends on the dynamics and operation time.

### The brain-energy comparison

At \(310\,\mathrm{K}\), the Landauer bound is \(2.967\times10^{-21}\,\mathrm{J/bit}\). A \(20\,\mathrm{W}\) power budget divided by this value gives a theoretical ceiling of \(6.74\times10^{21}\,\mathrm{bit/s}\), under the deliberately idealized assumption that all available power performs optimal bit erasure.

The event-rate range of \(10^{12}\)–\(10^{14}\) events/s is uncited in the supplied report and is a major determinant of the estimated gap. Moreover, the report’s three energy-per-event calculations do not agree:

- Dividing the \(20\,\mathrm{W}\) budget by the event-rate range gives \(2\times10^{-13}\) to \(2\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{J/event}\).
- A biophysical per-spike estimate gives \(10^{-14}\) to \(10^{-12}\,\mathrm{J}\).
- The figure band of \(10^{-14}\) to \(10^{-8}\,\mathrm{J/event}\) is arithmetically wrong.

Consequently, the gap should be retained only as a **[MODEL-DEPENDENT]** order-of-magnitude estimate, with uncertainty of approximately ±2–3 orders—not as a verified result.

### Biological interpretation and open measurement problem

Most of the brain’s approximately \(20\,\mathrm{W}\) is attributed to housekeeping, particularly maintenance of ion gradients by the Na/K-ATPase, rather than to logical bit erasure. The gap therefore mostly reflects the fraction of total metabolism assigned to housekeeping under the chosen accounting. It is not, on its own, a diagnostic of computational efficiency.
